svg.title: TCP buys reliability with round trips
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch with client and server timelines and the three-way handshake drawn as crossing arrows labelled SYN, SYN-ACK and ACK with a circled measured cost of 22.6 milliseconds, then four data segments where the second is crossed out in red mid-flight, a duplicate acknowledgement returns and the segment is retransmitted in green while everything behind it stalls; a bandwidth-delay-product pipe worked out as 1.22 megabytes in flight; and two lower panels showing a thousand small TCP sends coalescing into 413 differently sized reads against UDP datagrams drawn as sealed envelopes that keep their boundaries but two of which are crossed out as lost.
svg.text: TCP buys reliability with round trips
the handshake: 1 RTT before a single byte of data
then the data - and one segment goes missing
seg 3 arrives, but out of order
everything behind seg 2 waits. 1 loss = 1 RTT of stall for the whole stream.
Mathis: 100 ms RTT + 1% loss caps you at 1.4 Mbit/s, whatever your link says
TCP: a stream. Your message boundaries are GONE.
413 recv() calls. Up to 40 messages in ONE read.
recv. It is not, it never
